text_note.zh: 这里用《唐诗三百首》的通行文本，第二句作“来去九江侧”。另有版本作“去来九江侧”，意思一样。
text_note.en: This uses the common text from Three Hundred Tang Poems, where line two says lái qù, "coming and going". Another version says qù lái, "going and coming". The meaning is the same.

readings.zh: 长干：地名，“长”读 cháng，不读 zhǎng。
readings.en: In the place name Changgan, this is read cháng, not zhǎng.
In the place name Changgan, this is read gān.

glosses.en: lín: to be next to, close by.

glosses.zh: 九江：这里泛指长江下游一带的江水，不是今天江西的九江市。
glosses.en: jiǔ jiāng: here it means the lower Yangtze River in general, not today's city of Jiujiang in Jiangxi.
cè: beside, by the side of.

glosses.zh: 长干：地名，在今天江苏南京城南，靠近长江。
glosses.en: cháng gān: Changgan, a place in the south of today's Nanjing in Jiangsu, near the Yangtze.
xiāng shí: to know each other.

translation.en: My home is right beside the river,

translation.zh: 我常年在这江边来来往往。
translation.en: and I come and go along its banks.
So we are both from Changgan,

translation.zh: 可惜从小到大却不认识。
translation.en: yet we never knew each other growing up.

background.zh: 这是崔颢《长干曲》四首中的第二首，接着第一首往下说。第一首里，船上的姑娘问对方家在哪里，猜测是同乡。这一首是对方的回答：他也是长干人，常年在江上来往，只是两人从小不认识。两首连起来读，就像一问一答的对唱，很像民歌。写作的具体时间不清楚。
background.en: This is the second of Cui Hao's four Changgan Songs, and it carries on from the first. In the first, a young woman on a boat asks where the other person lives and guesses they are from the same place. This poem is the reply. He is also from Changgan and travels the river all year, but the two never knew each other as children. Read together, the two poems are like a question-and-answer duet, very much like a folk song. We do not know exactly when it was written.

author_note.zh: 崔颢（约704—754），唐代诗人，汴州（今河南开封）人。他最有名的诗是《黄鹤楼》，据说连李白看了都佩服。他早年的诗多写女子和爱情，后来到边塞走过，诗风变得雄浑。《长干曲》学的是南方民歌，语言像说话一样自然。
author_note.en: Cui Hao (about 704–754) was a Tang poet from Bianzhou, today's Kaifeng in Henan. His most famous poem is "Yellow Crane Tower"; it is said that even Li Bai admired it. His early poems were mostly about women and love. Later he travelled to the frontier, and his style grew bold and strong. His "Changgan Songs" copy the folk songs of the south, and the words are as natural as speech.

appreciation.zh: 这首诗是回答，也是感叹。前两句说：我家就住在江边，天天在江上来来往往。后两句说：原来我们都是长干人，可是从小到大竟然不认识！“同是”和“不相识”放在一起，有一种惊喜，也有一点可惜：这么近，却直到今天才在江上碰到。两首诗连起来，一个大胆地问，一个老实地答，没有写一句情话，却让人感觉到两个年轻人之间淡淡的好感。语言朴素，像江上人家平常说话一样。
appreciation.en: This poem is both a reply and a sigh. The first two lines say: my home is by the river, and I travel on it every day. The last two lines say: so we are both from Changgan, yet we never knew each other growing up! Putting "both from" next to "never knew" brings surprise and a little regret. They lived so close, but only met today on the river. Taken together, one person asks boldly and the other answers honestly. There is no word of love, yet we sense a gentle liking between two young people. The language is plain, like the everyday talk of river folk.
